items.headline: Game of the year? Bills outlast the Rams 37-34 in overtime
items.body: What a Monday nighter. Kyren Williams punched in a 1-yard score with four seconds left to force OT, then in overtime Greg Rousseau blocked a Rams field goal and Tyler Bass drilled a 45-yarder to win it. Josh Allen was a one-man wrecking crew — 210 passing yards, 121 rushing, and two touchdowns — as Buffalo moved to 4-1. People are already calling it a Super Bowl preview.
items.say: Did you catch that Bills-Rams game? Went to overtime, a blocked field goal, Josh Allen running all over the place — one of the best games I've seen all year.

items.headline: Guardians do it again — rally from 2-0 down to steal ALCS Game 1 in Tampa
items.body: These Guardians just will not quit. Trailing the top-seeded Rays 2-0, Cleveland erupted for seven runs over the final four innings — Chase DeLauter and catcher Patrick Bailey went deep, José Ramírez racked up three hits — to take Game 1 on the road, 7-3. Same comeback magic that buried the White Sox. Cleveland leads the pennant series 1-0.
items.say: The Guardians are unreal right now — down 2-0 in Tampa and they come all the way back to win Game 1. This team just refuses to lose. You got a team in it?

items.headline: Another giant falls — Carlos Alcaraz stunned in Shanghai
items.body: The upsets keep coming in China. Days after Djokovic went out early, world-beater Carlos Alcaraz was bounced by Belgium's Zizou Bergs — ranked way down the list — in straight sets (7-5, 7-6) in the third round. Bergs served lights-out for the biggest win of his career. The draw is now wide, wide open.
items.say: Tennis is a bloodbath in Shanghai — first Djokovic, now Alcaraz got knocked out by some guy nobody's heard of. Anybody can win it now. You follow tennis at all?

links.text: Alcaraz vs. Bergs — Shanghai highlights (Rolex Shanghai Masters)

items.headline: Dodgers and Brewers go again tonight — Milwaukee up 1-0
items.body: Over in the National League, the small-market, league-best Brewers grabbed Game 1 against the star-studded Dodgers and go for a 2-0 stranglehold tonight. It's the exact contrast October loves: L.A.'s deep-pocketed superstars against Milwaukee's scrappy, homegrown bunch. Winner of this one's halfway to the World Series.
items.say: Dodgers-Brewers Game 2 is on tonight — little-market Milwaukee's actually up on the big-money Dodgers. I kind of love rooting for the underdog. You watching any October baseball?

items.headline: The biggest night in soccer is coming — Ballon d'Or lands in London
items.body: With the club season on an international break, the soccer world's buzzing about the Ballon d'Or — the sport's top individual prize — which gets handed out Oct. 26. For the first time ever it's being held in London rather than Paris, and it's the 70th edition. This year's trophy honors the 2025-26 season, World Cup and all, so the debate over who deserves it is in full swing.
items.say: The Ballon d'Or's coming up — basically soccer's MVP award — and they moved it to London this year. Everybody's arguing about who should win. Who's your pick if you follow it?

items.headline: Jane Austen's back on the big screen — 'Sense and Sensibility' opens Friday
items.body: A lush new take on the Austen classic hits theaters Oct. 16, with Daisy Edgar-Jones ('Normal People') as the sensible Elinor and Esmé Creed-Miles as her heart-on-her-sleeve sister Marianne. Georgia Oakley directs for Focus Features, the same crew behind the beloved 'Pride & Prejudice' and 'Emma.' Pure cozy-sweater, fall-afternoon movie material.
items.say: There's a gorgeous-looking new Jane Austen movie out Friday — 'Sense and Sensibility,' with the 'Normal People' actress. Perfect fall date-night kind of film. You into the period-drama stuff, or not your thing?

links.text: TV Insider — inside the new Austen adaptation

items.headline: Something's in the water — Josh Hartnett's chiller 'Below' is streaming
items.body: Need a spooky-season binge? 'Below' just dropped on Netflix — a six-part supernatural thriller set on the foggy, windswept coast of Newfoundland, where a small town is menaced by something lurking offshore. Josh Hartnett, Charlie Heaton ('Stranger Things') and Mackenzie Davis lead it. Moody, atmospheric and perfect for a dark October night.
items.say: There's a creepy new Netflix show, 'Below' — Josh Hartnett, something in the water off a tiny coastal town. Looks like a great October binge. You need a new show, or already got one going?

items.headline: Back to Night City — 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2' drops next week
items.body: The anime that sent millions of people (back) into the 'Cyberpunk 2077' game is returning: Studio Trigger's 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2' premieres on Netflix Oct. 20, a brand-new 10-episode standalone story of revenge and redemption in neon-soaked Night City. The first one was a word-of-mouth sensation, so expect the internet to light up again.
items.say: That wild 'Cyberpunk' anime is getting a second season on Netflix next week — the first one blew up out of nowhere. You watch any of the grown-up animated stuff, or is that firmly the kids' department?

items.headline: Pour some sugar on 2027 — Def Leppard announce a huge tour with the Goo Goo Dolls
items.body: One for the classic-rock crowd: Def Leppard just announced a massive 45-date 2027 North American tour, with the Goo Goo Dolls and The Struts along for the ride, kicking off in March. They're even donating a dollar from every ticket to cancer charity City of Hope. General tickets go on sale this Friday (Oct. 16), so now's the time to grab the group chat.
items.say: Def Leppard just announced a big tour with the Goo Goo Dolls — tickets go on sale Friday. Might have to round up the crew for that one. You ever get out to the big nostalgia shows, or stick to the couch these days?
